name: The Fall of Ameth'Aran
summary: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade sends you to explore Ameth'Aran's ruins in Darkshore and read its ancient stone tablets. Their inscriptions tell of the Highborne city's ruin during the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

sections.title: Echoes of the Highborne
sections.body: Ameth'Aran was a flourishing settlement of Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who practiced powerful arcane magic. After the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city lay in broken marble and cracked pillars. Restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins.

sections.title: Uncovering Lost Chronicles
sections.body: Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact, as the War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed the ruins and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran. Ghostly Highborne specters forced her to retreat. The readings can carry the ancient disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

faq.answer: Ameth'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin in central Darkshore. Ten thousand years ago, it was a city where Queen Azshara's Highborne nobility wielded and studied powerful arcane magic before the Great Sundering brought its fall.

faq.q: Why are there ghosts in Ameth'Aran?
aliases: why are there spirits in ameth aran
faq.answer: The ghosts in Ameth'Aran are the spirits of the Highborne who lived and died there. The sudden catastrophe that shattered the Well of Eternity and fragmented Kalimdor bound them to the ruins in eternal torment.

aliases: who gives fall of ameth aran
faq.answer: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade is a night elf sentinel stationed along the road in Darkshore. She was tasked with scouting ancient sites and recovering lost historical records for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

faq.q: Why does the Circle of Ancients want these tablets read?
faq.answer: The Circle of Ancients wants the tablets read because the Well of Eternity's destruction plunged Kalimdor into immense upheaval, obliterating countless libraries and monuments. Few written records survived the War of the Ancients, so the tablets preserve rare firsthand Highborne accounts of the Sundering.

aliases: where are the ameth aran tablets
faq.answer: The Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran are etched into two large standing stone monuments among Ameth'Aran's ruined courtyards, surrounded by the wandering ghosts of the city's former residents.

faq.q: What happened to the Highborne of Ameth'Aran during the Sundering?
faq.answer: When the Well of Eternity imploded at the climax of the War of the Ancients, massive tremors and arcane backlash tore Kalimdor apart. Ameth'Aran collapsed, burying its citizens and leaving their ghosts in the rubble.

angles.text: As a night elf, you see Ameth'Aran's ruins as a grim reminder of your ancestors' hubris under Queen Azshara and the catastrophic consequences of unchecked arcane sorcery.
As a mage, you can read the tablets as a glimpse of pre-Sundering elven spellcraft at its height and the ruin that followed when that power spiraled out of control.
As an Alliance member, you help the Sentinels preserve Darkshore's history for the night elf leaders guiding the Alliance on Kalimdor.
